Question B-003-021-001.

Why the correct answer is right: UHF and microwave antennas can put concentrated RF close to sensitive tissue, so keeping active antennas away from eyes is conservative.

Per-choice notes:
- sourceIndex 0: "Keep antenna away from your eyes when RF is applied": This is the correct choice because UHF and microwave antennas can put concentrated RF close to sensitive tissue, so keeping active antennas away from eyes is conservative.
- sourceIndex 1: "Make sure that an RF leakage filter is installed at the antenna feed point": This is a near-miss because it shifts attention from Keep antenna away from your eyes when RF is applied. In RF exposure controls for UHF, microwave, handheld, indoor, dipole, and high-gain antennas, antenna details matter in station design, but this choice does not address the tested hazard or function.
- sourceIndex 2: "Make sure the standing wave ratio is low before you conduct a test": This answer would fit a different fault than Keep antenna away from your eyes when RF is applied. In RF exposure controls for UHF, microwave, handheld, indoor, dipole, and high-gain antennas, it names a different cause, control, component, or safety action than the one required here.
- sourceIndex 3: "Never use a horizontally polarized antenna": This option confuses another station topic with Keep antenna away from your eyes when RF is applied. In RF exposure controls for UHF, microwave, handheld, indoor, dipole, and high-gain antennas, antenna details matter in station design, but this choice does not address the tested hazard or function.
